# JTBD-### — Job Title

## Job Statement

> When **[situation / trigger]**, I want to **[motivation / action]**, so I can **[desired progress / outcome]**.

---

# 1. Job Summary

## Situation

Describe the circumstances in which the job becomes relevant.

**Trigger:**

What happened that caused the user to start making progress on this job?

**Context:**

- Property / space:
    
- Renovation stage:
    
- DIY / professional involvement:
    
- Time pressure:
    
- Budget pressure:
    
- Other constraints:
    

## Desired Progress

What progress is the user actually trying to make?

Avoid describing a Renovation Planner feature.

## Successful Outcome

The job is successfully fulfilled when:

---

# 2. Outcome Dimensions

## Functional Outcome

What practical result does the user need?

## Emotional Outcome

How does the user want to feel?

Examples:

- confident,
    
- in control,
    
- prepared,
    
- less uncertain,
    
- reassured.
    

## Social Outcome

How does the user want to be perceived by other people involved?

Examples:

- prepared when speaking to a contractor,
    
- reliable toward family members,
    
- knowledgeable when purchasing materials.
    

---

# 3. Forces of Progress

Use this section to understand why the user changes behavior rather than merely what they say they want.

## Push — Problems With the Current Situation

What makes the current situation unacceptable?

## Pull — Attraction of a Better Situation

What makes a better solution desirable?

## Anxiety — Concerns About Changing

What might prevent the user from adopting a different approach?

## Habit — Existing Behavior

What existing workflow or tool keeps the user doing things the current way?

# 9. Interview Prompts

Prefer questions about real past behavior.

## Trigger

> Tell me about the last time you needed to **[job]**.

> What happened that made you start thinking about this?

## Existing Process

> What did you do first?

> What happened next?

> What tools or information did you use?

## Decisions

> What choices did you have to make?

> What information did you need before you could decide?

## Friction

> What was the hardest part?

> Tell me about something that went wrong.

> Was there anything you had to redo?

## Alternatives

> How did you handle this before?

> What else did you consider doing?

## Consequences

> What happened because this was difficult?

> Did it cost additional time or money?

## Desired Outcome

> How did you know you were done?

> What would have made this significantly easier?

# 18. Product Assumptions Challenged

Does the research contradict anything currently assumed by the product?

Examples:

- Project → Space → Work hierarchy
    
- Project Home
    
- Next-Best-Action guidance
    
- Spaces vs Design separation
    
- floor-plan-first planning
    
- rough-estimate-first costing
    
- Work Package model
    
- trade-centric planning
    
- Open vs Continue
    

### Findings

If user evidence conflicts with the existing product model, record the conflict rather than forcing the evidence into the current architecture.
